newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION - LIONS TAKE FIRST OF THREE TOUGH STEPS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - LIONS TAKE FIRST OF THREE TOUGH STEPS.

text.p: The British Lions take the first of three steps to what they hope will be rugby heaven when they meet Northern Transvaal in the Afrikaner rugby cathedral of Loftus Versveld in Pretoria on Saturday.
It is followed by matches against Gauteng Lions (formerly Transvaal) on Wednesday and Currie Cup champions Natal next Saturday in a build-up to the first test.
"They will be like three test matches on their own," said Lions manager Fran Cotton.
"Every single match between now and the test will demand a little bit more of us. Each game has been a progression up the scale in difficulty -- Saturday will be very tough."
Northern Transvaal -- who will be without their five Springbok squad members -- had a poor Super 12, winning only three of their matches although they did draw at home with all-conquering Auckland.

They were the lowest placed of South Africa's four entrants finishing in eighth. Gauteng were fifth and Natal fourth while Free State -- whom the Lions play between the first and second tests -- finished seventh.

But they do represent the most serious challenge to a Lions side which has increasingly impressed local observers who were initially sceptical of the tourists ability to match southern hemisphere standards.
A tally of 22 tries from four successive victories has given the tourists a perfect start bar injuries which have forced the return home of lock Doddie Weir and flyhalf Paul Grayson.
England fly-half Mike Catt, who joined the squad as a replacement for Grayson on Wednesday, has been impressed already.

"Honestly, the atmosphere is unbelievable," he said. "The camaradarie, the way the players have gelled and the professionalism of the training -- especially with the rugby league chaps here -- has been superb."
Catt warms the bench alongside centre Scott Gibbs who has recovered from an ankle injury as the Lions try a new back row combination against the Blue Bulls.
Irish back rower Eric Miller gets the chance on the openside flank while Scott Quinnell starts his first match since the opening game of the tour at number eight.

The side otherwise shows only two changes from the one which defeated Western Province 38-21 last Saturday with Mark Regan coming in at hooker for Barry Williams and Ieuan Evans giving way to Tony Underwood on the right wing.

Northern Transvaal - 15-Graeme Bouwer, 14-Casper Steyn, 13-Johan Schutte, 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Wynand Lourens, 10-Roland de Marigny, 9-Conrad Breytenbach, 8-Adriaan Richter, 7-Schutte Bekker, 6-Nicky van der Walt, 5-Derrick Badenhorst, 4-Derrick Grobbelaar, 3-Piet Boer, 2-Henry Tromp, 1-Lourens Campher.
